checks: At each new fiber its own centroid translates by the same x_q as every point. The covariance numerator therefore scales by ε·ε^{2/d}, with no between-fiber term.
The old positive fibers make the covariance positive definite. Dividing by M+ε and differentiating the square root gives the uniform relative derivative −1/(2M) on the compact nonzero normal sets.
On each unchanged old fiber the two ramp kinks are volume-null for u≠0. The derivative at Γ_0=1 of f/Γ_ε is f/(2M), yielding A/(2M) with the stated negative sign.

Pullback to the fixed D_q gives the new contribution: the Lipschitz kernel changes by O(ε^{1/d}/h)+O(ε) on bounded marks for each of the finitely many fixed normals. Multiplication by ε gives the claimed uniform remainder. This is a positive fixed-h, fixed-cap result.

overlap.comparison: The accepted response covers actual uniformly radial paths on a fixed positive family. A new fiber of radius ε^{1/d} has no old positive boundary or radial speed in that formula. Here the covariance numerator and the born atomic capture are obtained directly.

readability: The separate letter h is fixed smoothing scale and does not shrink with the birth parameter.
summary: The pooled covariance change and the exact fixed-cap derivative are correct for a mass-parametrized birth and fixed positive ramp width.
